blocks.content: Grafana turns Prometheus's stored time-series data into actual, visual dashboards, and it typically runs as nothing more exotic than an ordinary application inside the very cluster it is monitoring.

Where Prometheus, covered in the previous topic, collects and stores metrics, Grafana is what turns that raw time-series data into actual graphs, charts, and dashboards a human can meaningfully look at and understand.

blocks.alt: Turning raw stored metrics into something a human can actually read and understand

blocks.content: 2. Deployed as an Ordinary Kubernetes App
blocks.text: 2. Deployed as an Ordinary Kubernetes App

blocks.content: This is worth appreciating directly, Grafana is not special, privileged infrastructure, it commonly runs as an entirely ordinary Deployment, exposed through a Service and often an Ingress, exactly the same object types covered throughout this course.

blocks.alt: Nothing special, just an ordinary Deployment and Service like any other app

blocks.content: Real Grafana dashboards in a Kubernetes context commonly cover cluster-wide health (node resource usage, Pod counts), and application-specific metrics (request rates, error rates, latency), giving a genuinely visual view of the entire system's behavior over time.

blocks.alt: Cluster health and application metrics, both made genuinely visual and understandable

blocks.content: Put together with everything else covered in this module, the full Kubernetes observability toolkit spans live, ad-hoc tools (kubectl logs, describe, exec, top, covered earlier in this module) and historical, visual tools (Prometheus and Grafana), each answering a genuinely different kind of question.

blocks.alt: Live, ad-hoc tools and historical, visual tools, together forming the complete picture

blocks.content: Exactly like Prometheus, this topic covers Grafana specifically in its Kubernetes context, full depth on dashboard design, data sources, and alerting is covered in the dedicated Monitoring & Logging category.

blocks.alt: The Kubernetes-specific framing here, the complete depth in its own dedicated category

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Grafana visualizes Prometheus's time-series data as real dashboards, and typically runs as nothing more than an ordinary Deployment and Service inside the cluster.
Together, kubectl's live tools and Prometheus/Grafana's historical, visual tools form the complete Kubernetes observability picture, each answering a genuinely different kind of question.
